title: Sales Enablement Playbook: Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pitch Decks, Pricing Guidance, Case Studies & Security FAQ
author: Avery Chen
content:
Overview

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference’s recommended positioning, competitive briefing templates, pitch-deck checklist, pricing guidance, representative case studies, and a buyer-facing Security & Compliance FAQ. It is intended for AE/SDR/SE teams and should be used as the canonical source for go-to-market messaging, deal-level objections, and pre-sales security conversations.

Owners and signal paths
- Primary owner: Go-to-Market enablement (owner_team: go-to-market).
- Content reviewers: Product, Security, Legal, and Solutions Engineering.
- For updates: submit PR through the enablement content repo and request review from the listed reviewers.

1) Positioning & Core Messaging

Summary statement (one-liner): Redwood Inference provides a developer-first inference platform that makes high-performance, reliable LLM serving predictable and economical across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Key value pillars (talk tracks):
- Production-first performance: predictable latency and throughput (P95 targets, deterministic capacity) so engineering teams ship reliable LLM features.
- Cost & economics: tooling and controls (batching, KV caching, quantization profiles, routing policies) that materially reduce per-token cost while preserving quality.
- Deployment flexibility: same API and operational tooling across Hosted API, Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), and Private (VPC / on-prem) deployments.
- Reliability & graceful degradation: multiple fallbacks—model variants, regional routing, and tiered capacity—to keep customer applications online during spikes or failures.
- Enterprise readiness: SLAs, audit logging, KMS/HSM integrations, and compliance evidence for regulated customers.

Audience-specific positioning
- Engineers/ML: emphasize runtime internals, kernel selection, KV-cache, batching, and model versioning APIs.
- Platform/Infra: emphasize predictable capacity, autoscaling controls, dedicated pools, and integration with existing observability stacks.
- Product/PM: emphasize predictable UX, latency SLOs, rollout policies, and quality monitoring tied to prompt sets.

2) Competitive Brief Template (use per-deal)

Use this template to create a 1-page competitive brief for each named competitor or customer concern. Fill in the sections below and attach as a slide in proposals.
- Competitor: [name]
- Typical customer use cases they win with: [short list]
- Strengths: [1–3 bullets]
- Weaknesses / key differentiators for Redwood: [1–3 bullets with evidence]
- Deal playbook / objection handling: 1–3 recommended scripts or technical rebuttals
- Technical comparators to include: latency P50/P95 numbers, batching/throughput limits, quantization support, private deployment options, SLA and security certifications, pricing model differences (per-token vs reserved), integration surface (SDKs, tracing hooks)

Example competitor notes (summary):
- Cloud Vendor X: Strength — deep integration with cloud provider tooling; Weakness — higher per-token cost at scale, limited on-prem offering, fewer inference optimizations for large context LLMs. Playbook — emphasize Redwood’s predictable dedicated offering, lower unit economics for steady throughput, and Private deployment capabilities.

3) Pitch Deck Checklist (pre-assembled slides to tailor per prospect)

Required slides (order recommended):
1. Title / one-line value prop (use the summary statement).
2. Problem statement and customer pain (latency, cost, reliability, rollout risk).
3. How Redwood solves it (high-level architecture and deployment modes).
4. Key features & differentiators (runtime optimizations, routing, caching, rollouts).
5. Performance & economics (benchmarks vs open models and cloud offerings; include P50/P95 latency table and cost delta for a sample workload).
6. Security & compliance (SOC 2, encryption, VPC/private options, audit logging).
7. Deployment models & pricing overview (Hosted API / Dedicated / Private).
8. Case study (relevant vertical).
9. Implementation plan & timeline (pilot -> production).
10. Next steps & CTA (trial, pilot contract, tech deep-dive).

Deck best practices:
- Include one slide with concrete benchmark numbers (same workload across comparators). Always cite test harness and workload parameters (sequence length, batch size, model family, tokenization).
- Tailor the case study to the prospect’s vertical and the main decision-maker (engineering vs procurement).
- Keep pricing examples simple—use a single representative workload to show unit economics and TCO over 12 months.

4) Pricing Guidance (sales guidance / playbook)

Pricing model overview (how to discuss with customers):
- Hosted API: usage-based pricing (per-token generation/embedding units) for fast time-to-value and experimentation. Good for low-volume and variable workloads.
- Dedicated: reserved capacity (monthly/annual commits) for predictable steady throughput; pricing is based on committed GPU capacity with overage and burst options.
- Private: platform fee + optional support license and on-prem packaging for air-gapped or regulated environments.

Discounting & packaging rules (recommended guardrails):
- Trial/POC credits: standard 90-day sandbox credits. For pilots >3 months, consider a pilot pricing discount (10–25%) tied to clear success metrics.
- Enterprise discounts: volume and term-based. Use list-price as anchor, escalate to sales leadership for discounts >35%.
- Dedicated commits: require minimum 3-month commitment; standard negotiation range for enterprise customers is 6–36 months.
- Bundled observability / retention: treat as add-on; promote 12-month retention as default for mid-market, 36-month for enterprise for additional fee.

Example pricing talk track (engineering audience):
- "For latency-sensitive, steady workloads we recommend Redwood Dedicated. For a 100M tokens/month steady workload, our analysis shows a 30–55% lower TCO compared to generic cloud endpoints once batching and caching are applied—this is driven by reserved GPU utilization and quantization profiles tailored per workload."

Approval matrix and deal desk triggers:
- Discounts >20% or multi-year deals require approval from Sales Leader and Finance.
- Dedicated > $100k ARR or Private deals require Legal and Security sign-off before term-sheet.

5) Case Studies (representative snippets for pitch decks)

Include 2–3 short, proof-oriented case studies that map to common verticals (SaaS, healthcare, finance). Each case study should be 4–6 bullet points and include concrete outcomes (latency, cost, time-to-production), owner contact, and short quote.

Case study: AtlasHealth (healthcare SaaS)
- Problem: inconsistent inference latency and data residency requirements for PHI processing.
- Redwood solution: Private deployment with KMS integration and audit logging; model pinned to v1.4 with quantized runtime.
- Outcome: 55% reduction in per-token cost vs prior managed endpoints, P95 latency reduced from 620ms to 210ms, SOC2 attestation supported compliance review.
- Timeline: pilot (4 weeks) -> production (8 weeks).
- Reference: Lydia Park, Director of ML Engineering (lydia.park@atlashealth.example).

Case study: CommerceAI (e‑commerce personalization)
- Problem: poor throughput and unpredictable unit costs during seasonal spikes.
- Redwood solution: Dedicated GPU pools with autoscaling and burst policies; prefix caching for repeated prompts.
- Outcome: steady 3x throughput improvement during peak windows, estimated 40% lower TCO across peak months, zero customer-facing downtime during holiday season.
- Reference: Omar Singh, Head of Product (omar.singh@commerceai.example).

6) Security & Compliance FAQ for Prospects (concise answers for sales and SEs)

Q: What certifications and attestations does Redwood have?
A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certifications. For enterprise customers we provide compliance evidence under an NDA and maintain a documented compliance roadmap for additional regimes (e.g., HIPAA readiness via Private deployments).

Q: How is customer data protected in transit and at rest?
A: All network traffic is TLS 1.2+ in transit. Data at rest is encrypted with AES-256. Key management is supported via customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM integrations) for Dedicated and Private deployments.

Q: Can customers run Redwood in their VPC or on-prem?
A: Yes. Private deployments are available for VPC and on-prem air-gapped installations. Private mode includes a customer-managed control plane option and supports on-prem packaging with documented installation and upgrade procedures.

Q: How do you support data residency and retention requirements?
A: We offer regionally isolated deployment options and configurable retention policies. For Hosted API customers, retention defaults are documented in the data-retention policy and can be adjusted for enterprise contracts. Private deployments enable full customer control over storage retention.

Q: What audit and logging capabilities exist?
A: Detailed audit logs (API, auth, admin actions) are available and can be routed to customer SIEMs. We provide per-token request traces and model-route mappings for forensic analysis. Logs are tamper-evident and can be exported for compliance reviews.

Q: How is isolation between customers enforced?
A: Isolation mechanisms include dedicated GPU pools (Dedicated), VPC isolation, tenant-level RBAC, encrypted KV caches, and network policy enforcement. Cross-tenant access requires explicit RBAC policies and is prevented by default.

Q: Do you allow penetration testing or security assessments?
A: Yes. We have a coordinated pentest process. For Hosted customers we provide an approved scope and timeline; enterprise customers on Dedicated or Private can run bespoke assessments under an MOU.

Q: What contractual security controls are available?
A: Standard SLAs, data processing agreements (DPAs), Business Associate Agreements (BAAs) for HIPAA workflows (Private deployments), and custom security addenda can be negotiated for enterprise deals.

7) Sales Playbook & Objection Handling (short scripts)

Objection: "We can build this ourselves."
Response: "Building and operating a production-grade inference stack requires sustained investment in kernel optimization, autoscaling logic, monitoring, and security. Redwood provides a unified runtime, continuous batching and KV caching, and production SLAs so your team can focus on product features rather than ops. Typical customer TCO shows large savings after 3–6 months vs a DIY approach when factoring engineering cost and time-to-market."

Objection: "We’re concerned about vendor lock-in."
Response: "Redwood’s API and deployment abstraction allow you to pin model versions and move between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. We provide data export tools and clear operational runbooks to minimize migration friction."

8) Implementation Plan Examples (pilot -> production)

Standard pilot (6–8 weeks):
1) Discovery & success criteria (week 0–1)
2) Pilot setup (Hosted or Dedicated sandbox) and baseline benchmarking (week 1–2)
3) Integration & iteration (prompt tuning, KV caching) (week 2–4)
4) Performance optimization & security review (week 4–6)
5) Production cutover plan & runbook handoff (week 6–8)

Enterprise rollout considerations:
- Security sign-off (Legal & Security) and contract finalization before production traffic.
- Capacity reservations and autoscaling policy finalization prior to go-live.
- SLA and monitoring integration (PagerDuty, Datadog, Splunk) configured and tested.

10) Appendix: Messaging Snippets (copy/paste for outreach)

- Short email opener (for engineering contact): "Hi [name], Redwood Inference helps teams reduce inference cost and P95 latency by combining a GPU-optimized runtime with caching and smart routing—can we run a 2-week pilot and show a 30%+ cost improvement for your top gen workloads?"
- Exec-level one-liner: "Redwood Inference makes LLM serving predictable and economical so product teams ship faster without sacrificing reliability or security."
- Security-oriented outreach: "We offer Private deployments and on-prem packaging with KMS integrations, SOC 2 Type II attestations, and audit logs to support your compliance needs—can we schedule a 30-minute security deep-dive?"
